```
    [ ] B2b — add regression test
  [!] B3 — Avatar upload 500s over 5MB (blocked: needs S3 creds from ops)

Features
  [ ] F1 — Dark mode
  [ ] F2 — Bulk delete in the table view
  [?] F3 — Pick the chart library [decide: @asha]

Agent-found
  [ ] A1 — Unhandled promise rejection in the upload worker
  [>] A2 — `parseDate` returns Invalid Date on empty string (deferred: after the parser rewrite)

7 open (4 pending · 1 in-progress · 0 testing · 1 blocked · 1 pending decision) · 1 deferred · 9 closed (8 done · 1 cancelled) · 17 total
```

### By status (`list tickets status`)

Same lines, regrouped. Sections in this order — **in-progress first**, because
that is what someone asking for a status view wants to see — In progress,
Testing, Blocked, Pending decision, Deferred, Pending (this board has nothing
under test, so no Testing section):

```
In progress
  [~] B2 — CSV export drops the last row

Blocked
  [!] B3 — Avatar upload 500s over 5MB (blocked: needs S3 creds from ops)

Pending decision
  [?] F3 — Pick the chart library [decide: @asha]

Deferred
  [>] A2 — `parseDate` returns Invalid Date on empty string (deferred: after the parser rewrite)

Pending
  [ ] B2b — add regression test (B2)
  [ ] F1 — Dark mode
  [ ] F2 — Bulk delete in the table view
  [ ] A1 — Unhandled promise rejection in the upload worker

7 open (4 pending · 1 in-progress · 0 testing · 1 blocked · 1 pending decision) · 1 deferred · 9 closed (8 done · 1 cancelled) · 17 total
```

A sub-part shown away from its parent carries the parent ID in trailing
parentheses — `(B2)` — since the indentation that explained it is gone. Include
`Done` and `Cancelled` sections only when closed tickets were asked for.

### Rules for both views

- **Copy the line, don't rewrite it.** ID and title exactly as they appear in
  `TICKETS.md`, so the user can grep for what they just read.
- **Never collapse a ticket to its ID.** `A295 A297 A299 A301` is not a board,
  it is a receipt — the reader has to grep every number to learn anything, which
  is the exact work the list was supposed to save. A ticket line is **ID + title,
  always**, no matter how many there are. A long title truncates at ~80 chars
  with `…`; it never disappears. If the board is too long to print, **page it —
  never abbreviate it** (below).
- **Open and deferred, by default** (`[ ]`, `[~]`, `[%]`, `[!]`, `[?]`, `[>]`) — every
  deferred ticket is listed, just counted apart. Closed tickets on request
  ("show everything", "what did we finish") — then `[x]` and `[-]` too.
- **Drop empty sections.** No "Features: none", no empty `Blocked`.
- **Blocked and deferred show their reason**; that is the whole point of
  `[!]` and `[>]`. Pending decision shows who decides — its `[decide: ..]` tag;
  testing shows what test — its `(testing: ..)` note.
- **The counts must add up, and the line must show its work.** Eight mutually
  exclusive states, two buckets and a loner:
  `open = pending + in-progress + testing + blocked + pending decision`
  (testing, blocked and pending decision are open, just waiting) ·
  `closed = done + cancelled` · deferred is **neither** — it stands alone
  between them, so it never inflates the open count someone is judging the
  week by · `total = open + deferred + closed`. Each bucket prints its own
  subtotal with the breakdown in parentheses, so the arithmetic is checkable on
  sight and blocked is never mistaken for a bucket beside open.
- **Always print all eight states, zeros included.** Never drop a term because
  it is `0`. `0 blocked` is information — it says nothing is stuck, which is
  exactly what someone scanning the board wants to know — and a fixed-shape line
  can be compared against last session's at a glance. An empty board still
  prints the full line:

  ```
  0 open (0 pending · 0 in-progress · 0 testing · 0 blocked · 0 pending decision) · 0 deferred · 0 closed (0 done · 0 cancelled) · 0 total
  ```
- **One count line after the list**, and nothing else. No commentary on the
  board's health, no suggested next ticket unless asked:

  ```
  7 open (4 pending · 1 in-progress · 0 testing · 1 blocked · 1 pending decision) · 1 deferred · 9 closed (8 done · 1 cancelled) · 17 total
  ```
- Legend only if the user seems new to the board, and then one line.

### Big boards (30+ open)

Long boards are where the list is *most* needed and most often ruined. Do not
compress by dropping titles. Compress by **showing less of the board, in full**:

1. **In-progress, testing, blocked and pending decision print in full, always.** However big the board,
   that is what the person asking is actually working on and stuck behind.
2. **Pending prints in full up to 20 lines per section**, oldest first. Over
   that, print 20 and add one line naming the rest and how to see it:

   ```
   … 24 more pending in Agent-found — `list tickets A` for all of them
   ```
3. **Group by ID prefix, not by the heading the line sits under.** Append-only
   files drift: a `B68` logged during a burst of agent findings ends up under
   `## Agent-found` and stays there forever. The ID is the classification; the
   heading is just where the line happened to land. Sort within a group by status
   (in-progress, testing, blocked, pending decision, deferred, pending) then by number.
4. **`list tickets <prefix>`** (`list tickets A`, `list tickets B`) scopes to one
   type and prints it whole, no cap. That is the escape hatch the truncation line
   points at, so it must actually work.

The count line stays exactly the same — it already covers the whole board, which
is what makes truncating the list safe.

## Rules

- **One file, repo root, committed.** It travels with the branch; that is how
  teammates and future chats see it.
- **Append, never rewrite.** New tickets go at the end of their section; edits
  touch only the one line being changed. Keeps merge conflicts to single lines.
- **IDs are permanent.** No reuse, no renumbering, no deleting done tickets —
  delete a ticket only if it was logged in error (say so to the user). The one
  move is a merge collision, done by `renumber-tickets.sh`, ` (was X)` kept.
- **Committed and pushed with the work.** The board travels in the same commit
  as the change, never left behind locally.
- **Every edit is signed.** Create or flip a row, stamp your session tag on it,
  replacing the old one. An unsigned flip on a shared board is unattributable.
- **Status reflects reality.** `[x]` means verified, not "should work". `[-]`
  means deliberately closed without doing it — never use it to hide a ticket
  that is still real, and `[!]` is not a parking space: it names what it waits on.
- **The board must drain.** A ticket is a named change, never a finding — see
  the gate. If pending only ever grows, the bookkeeping has become the work:
  stop logging and run the drain.

# build-jarvis — every feature, graded, designed, built

The one build skill. It **is** `PRACTICE.md` §§1-6 for a feature, design
included, so nothing runs in front of it — not `superpowers:brainstorming`, not
`writing-plans`, not a second `build-*`. You are the **orchestrator**: you grade,
dispatch, rule and keep the record. Design and code run in subagents, each with
an explicit model, because a skill cannot change the main session's model.

Read **`PRACTICE.md`** first — beside `PLATFORMS.md`, at the plugin root (`../`
in the `install.sh` layout, `../../` in a checkout or the plugin cache). It owns
classification, questions, the TASKS shape, self-review, test-first, evidence
and review. Everything below assumes it.

## Step 0 — GRADE, before anything is spent

0. **Not a build after all?** A request that only changes how an existing
   screen looks or reads - polish, redesign, critique, fonts/colours/spacing/
   contrast, "less generic", UX copy, an a11y pass, a frame that draws wrong -
   with no new behaviour, or one that names design-arwen / tui-tron, is handed
   straight to that skill: one line `ui-only -> design-arwen` (or `tui-tron`),
   load it, no grade line, no design file. This is the one Step 0 exit that
   prints no `grade:` line (the grade gate guards Write and Agent only; a Skill
   call is not gated, so the hand-off passes).
1. **Classify** spike / bounded / architectural (PRACTICE §1).
2. **Criticality.** The work is **critical** when it touches auth, money,
   concurrency, or a contract others depend on (a shared API, a file format, a
   schema). Say which word made it critical.
3. **Tier each seat** from this table — the same one as `practice/task-loop.md`
   § Model selection and `tickets-zordon`'s scout:

   | The work reads like | design | build | verify |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | One file, mechanical, the change is named | — | cheap | build |
   | 1-2 files, complete spec, nothing left to decide | — | cheap | build |
   | Several files, integration, or choices left open | deep | build | build |
   | Cause unknown, design judgement, architectural | deep | build | deep |
   | Critical (any row) | deep | build | **deep, held** |

   Critical's build seat is the **build** tier (`build=opus` on Claude Code,
   per `PLATFORMS.md`), never cheap.

   `—` = no design pass: the request or ticket *is* the spec, and you write it
   into the design file as its one task. **build is the floor** for every verify
   seat and for a build seat working from prose rather than named code.

   **ui** - `arwen` (web/native surface), `tron` (terminal UI), `none`; the
   field sits between ceremony and mode
   ([references/grade.md § The ui field](references/grade.md#the-ui-field)).
4. **Tier → model:** read `.skillator/tiers.local.md` (written by
   `grayskull-power`'s `tiers` arm step). Missing → the first slug in your
   host's column of `PLATFORMS.md` § Role tiers, and say `tiers: defaults`.
5. **Step down, never up on your own** — the one exception is Phase 2's
   third fix round, and only with its `Ruling:` line:
   - a tier whose model the file marks `down:` → that seat goes one tier lower;
   - usage ≥ 70 % of the 5-hour window (`watch-cortana`'s `usage-watch.* level`,
     the `5h=` field) → every **non-critical** seat one tier lower; `src=none`
     → no step-down, and say `usage unobservable`;
   - never below cheap, never a verify seat below build, and a **held** seat
     keeps the highest tier still available.
   Every downgrade is a line: `Ruling: <seat> <from>-><to> - <why> - <cost if wrong>`.
6. **User words win over the table** (unavailability still wins over them):
   "use fable" / "fable designs" → design and deep seats on fable · "opus only"
   / "all opus" → every seat opus · "cheap" / "on a budget" → every
   non-critical seat one tier lower · "top tier" / "best models" → every seat
   deep · a named model → that seat on it.
7. **Your first reply text after loading this skill is the grade line** —
   before the design-file Write, before any Agent call. No confirmation gate
   (step 8's mode question is the one Step 0 ask); the line is there so the
   user can overrule before the first token is spent:

   ```
   grade: bounded · critical no · design - · build cheap=sonnet · verify build=opus · ceremony lean · ui none · mode ask (single) · usage 5h 41%
   ```

   **Printed means reply text the user sees**, starting `grade:`, before the
   design file is written or anything is dispatched. A grade worked out in your
   thinking, a `Ruling: critical no` in the design file, or a summary at the
   end is not printed — the user cannot overrule a line they never saw.

   **The line is a required input.** It is the design file's first line and
   the first line of every Agent prompt (design, build, verify), verbatim. So
   whichever spend comes first — the design-file Write *or* a design agent —
   print the line as reply text, then paste the same line into that call.
8. **Mode — the grade line's `mode` field, settled before any spend.** How
   Phase 2 runs:

   | Mode | What runs | Fits |
   |---|---|---|
   | **single** | One build agent does every task in order; design and verify stay their own seats | `—` design seat, 1-3 tightly coupled tasks, tasks sharing files |
   | **per-task** | One fresh build agent per task (`tasks-sentinels`); same-file tasks never fan out | Several independent tasks — the usual pick when nothing else fits |
   | **workflow** | Phases 1-3 as one workflow script (`WORKFLOW.md`); no `Workflow` tool → the host's parallel subagents | 4+ independent tasks or a sweep — costs the most tokens |

   - `mode ask (<recommended>)` — the default. Right after the grade line, ask
     once: all three modes, your recommendation first (`AskUserQuestion`; no
     such tool → a numbered list). Then **end your turn** — no design-file
     Write, no Agent, until the user answers. Then reprint the line with
     `mode <m> (asked)`; that line is the one the design file and every
     Agent prompt carry.
   - `mode <m> (named)` — the user already named one ("single agent", "one
     agent per task", "use a workflow", "ultracode"). No question.
   - `mode <m> (ruled)` — the prompt or run says headless, chained or inside a
     relay. No question; log `Ruling: mode <m> - <why> - <cost if wrong>`.
     A bare feature request is not headless, whatever tools you lack.

   Recommend from the grade row and how coupled the work reads. **Never
   workflow without the user's opt-in**: unasked, the most you pick is per-task.

**Ceremony** is `full` when the work is architectural, has 4+ tasks, runs
inside a relay run, or is said to outlive this session ("keep going after",
"hand it over", "full ceremony"); otherwise `lean`. Full adds the session
record, the handoff checkpoint, the TRACE table and the rework loop —
**[references/ceremony.md](references/ceremony.md)**.

Grade detail, the tiers file, the unavailable-at-dispatch retry and worked
examples: **[references/grade.md](references/grade.md)**.

## Design questions — ruled or parked, never asked mid-build

- **Decidable** from the repo, the ticket, PRACTICE or a stated rule → rule it
  and write it into the design file's `## Decisions`:
  `Ruling: <what> - <why> - <cost if wrong>`.
- **Only the user can answer** (taste, a fact only they hold, a conflict nothing
  settles) → `relay-morpheus park`, and build everything that does not depend on
  it. A relay run in flight → park on its stage. A standalone build → open a
  one-stage run first so the park has a home (commands in
  [references/grade.md](references/grade.md#parking-from-a-standalone-build)).
- **The six stops** (destructive op, security-sensitive action, a side effect
  outside this worktree, the 7-day limit at 90 %, a scope breach, a failed
  repro) → ask now, alone.
- **Architectural** keeps PRACTICE §1's one approval gate after the design is
  written and reviewed — asked when the user is present, parked when the run is
  headless, chained or the user is away.
- "ask me as you go", "brainstorm with me", "let's design it together" →
  live questions instead, one at a time (PRACTICE §1); each answer still lands
  in `## Decisions`.

## Phase 1 — Design

Design seat `—` → write the design file yourself from the request. Otherwise
dispatch one design agent on the design seat's model with the request verbatim,
the repo context and `PRACTICE.md`; it writes the file and returns only its path
plus two lines:

```
grade: <the Step 0 line, verbatim - also already printed as reply text>
GOAL:         <the task in one line>
CHOSEN:       <the approach + why; architectural lists 2-3 APPROACHES first>
DESIGN:       <data model / contracts, key edge cases, out of scope>
CONSTRAINTS:  <what stays true across every task - exact values, names,
              formats; copied verbatim into every reviewer as
              [GLOBAL_CONSTRAINTS]>
TASKS:        <one block per task in PRACTICE §2 shape (Files, Interfaces,
              test-first steps with real code and commands), each tagged
              build=<tier> from the Step 0 table>
VERIFICATION: <the exact end-to-end command and its expected output>
## Decisions  <every Ruling: made so far; parked questions by Q-id>
```

Lean: `design-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` in the scratchpad. Full:
`docs/sessions/session-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md`, plus the REQUIREMENTS / TRACE
slots in [references/ceremony.md](references/ceremony.md).

This core design is architecture, interfaces and workflow - no UI craft; a UI
task block says only what the surface must do (states, data, keys), not how it
looks.

**UI design pass** (`ui` not `none`) — after the core file is written: one
agent on the design seat's model (a `—` seat: the build seat's) with this
prompt:

```
<grade line verbatim>
Load skillator:design-arwen (mode build for a new surface, improve for a change to one) and read the design file at <path> first. Design the UI for the TASKS that touch a surface, on top of the core design - never change DESIGN, CONSTRAINTS or the interfaces. Append a section `## UI design` (the signature, screens/states, hierarchy, platform notes, the a11y floor) and rewrite each UI task block's steps so an implementer builds that design (real code, test-first). Return the file path and the section's first line.
```

`ui tron`: the same prompt with `Load skillator:tui-tron`, and the section holds
the width matrix (the widths the app must draw at), the capture command per
width and the frame each must show; those captures go into VERIFICATION as the
render proof. Ops-board pane work: its `claude plugin test` frame assertions
are the render proof; a width matrix only for the standalone ops app.
`ui arwen+tron`: two passes, arwen first.

Then self-review once (PRACTICE §3), both sections, and fix inline. A
`ui tron` VERIFICATION without the captured frames is unmet (Phase 3). A
**spike** stops at Phase 1: the probe and a recommendation, nothing kept.

## Phase 2 — Build

The Step 0.8 mode decides the shape. **per-task**: one agent per task, each on
its own tagged tier; independent tasks fan out, same-file tasks do not.
**single**: one build agent takes every task block in order, on the highest
tagged tier, and reports per block. Either way a build agent gets fresh context,
the **design file path** and its task block(s) — never the design pasted, never
this session's history (PRACTICE §4; procedure `practice/task-loop.md`, prompt
text `practice/prompts.md`). Several F tickets are one pass, one task block per
ticket; a build agent implements its block(s) only — it never loads this skill,
regrades or runs its own verify. Review each block against its spec before the
next dispatch; a failed review goes to a fix agent. A third round may go one
tier up, and only with
`Ruling: <seat> <from>-><to> - reviews <1> and <2> failed: <why each failed> - <cost if wrong>`
citing both failed reviews; no Ruling, no step up.

**Mode workflow** (the user opted in) → run Phases 1-3 as one workflow script
(`WORKFLOW.md`): write the design file first, pass its path in `args`, and the
build stage reads each task's tier: `model: M[t.build]`.

## Phase 3 — Verify, review, relay

Run VERIFICATION through PRACTICE §5 — the command, now, in full, exit code
read — on the verify seat. Anything bigger than bounded, or critical, gets one
whole-diff review on the verify seat's tier (PRACTICE §6,
`code-review:code-review`). Failures go back through Phase 2's fix loop. Then
relay: the grade line again as the report's first line, what was built
(files), the verification evidence, every Ruling, every parked Q-id.

## Rules

- **Grade before spending.** No design file, no dispatch, before the grade
  line is printed as reply text.
- **A budget is a step-down, never a merge.** A spend cap (`--max-budget-usd`,
  "on a budget", a cost ceiling) means "cheap" — every non-critical seat one
  tier lower, said in a `Ruling:`. It never reaches critical work: critical
  keeps its deep design seat (a dispatched design agent) and its deep, held
  verify. It never folds the seats into this session:
  a subagent costs no more than the same work done here, and the orchestrator
  that builds has nobody to verify it.

| Rationalization | Reality |
|---|---|
| "I graded it — it's in my reasoning / the design file's Rulings." | Not printed. The line exists so the user can overrule it before spend; invisible, it overrules nothing. |
| "Small and obvious; the grade line is ceremony." | It is one line. Size does not waive it; `design -` already says it was small. |
| "The budget won't cover subagents, so I'll design, build and verify here." | Same tokens, minus the second pair of eyes. Step seats down; keep them separate. |
| "Critical work — safer if I do it all myself." | Critical makes verify **deep, held**: a different seat, not this one. |
| "The cap reads as cheap, so the critical design seat drops to build." | The step-down is for non-critical seats only. Critical design stays deep and dispatched. |

**Red flag:** about to Write the design file, or call Agent — a design agent
included — with no `grade:` line in your reply text yet, or with `mode ask`
still unanswered: stop and print or ask first. Critical work is no exception;
it is where the overrule matters most.
- **Never an unnamed model.** An omitted model inherits the session's.
- **The design file is the handover.** Pass it by path; the orchestrator does
  not design or code, bar writing a `—`-seat design file and the record.
- **Autonomous, honest.** A phase that fails or an agent that returns nothing is
  said plainly; nothing continues on a missing piece.
- **Handoff before context loss.** About to `/compact` or `/clear` → run
  `handoff-cortana` first.

## Other hosts

`PLATFORMS.md` turns tiers into slugs and dispatch into the host's delegate
mechanism; no delegation → run the seats sequentially in one session, each
phase's output written to disk before the model switch. Per-host notes, the
seat table and the Opus-version limit: [references/platforms.md](references/platforms.md).
The `UserPromptSubmit` route hook that puts a feature prompt here on Claude
Code: [references/route-hook.md](references/route-hook.md).

import argparse

from shelf import books, report


def main(argv=None):
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="shelf")
    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    a = sub.add_parser("add")
    a.add_argument("title")
    a.add_argument("author")
    f = sub.add_parser("find")
    f.add_argument("query")
    sub.add_parser("report")
    args = p.parse_args(argv)
    if args.cmd == "add":
        books.add(args.title, args.author)
    elif args.cmd == "find":
        for b in books.find(args.query):
            print("%s - %s" % (b["title"], b["author"]))
    else:
        print(report.summary())
    return 0

GOAL: `python -m shelf serve` serves a small local web page where a member picks
the default sort of `list` (title or author); the choice is saved to disk and
`python -m shelf list` uses it on later runs.

CHOSEN: stdlib only (`http.server`, `json`, `pathlib`) — the project has no
dependencies and no build. A new `shelf/settings.py` owns load/save of a JSON
file; a new `shelf/web.py` owns the HTTP handler; `cli.py` gains `list` and
`serve`. `list` does not exist yet, so it is added here (it is the thing the
setting controls).

DESIGN:
- `shelf/settings.py`
  - `SORT_KEYS = ("title", "author")`, `DEFAULTS = {"sort": "title"}`
  - `path()` → `Path(os.environ["SHELF_SETTINGS"])` if set, else
    `Path.home() / ".shelf" / "settings.json"`.
  - `load()` → dict: DEFAULTS merged with the file. Missing file, unreadable
    file, invalid JSON, or a `sort` value not in SORT_KEYS → that key falls back
    to its default (never raises).
  - `save(sort)` → validates (`ValueError` if not in SORT_KEYS), creates the
    parent dir, writes `{"sort": sort}` as UTF-8 JSON atomically (write a temp
    file in the same dir, then `os.replace`). Returns the saved dict.
- `shelf/books.py`: `sorted_books(key)` → `sorted(all_books(), key=lambda b: b[key].casefold())`;
  `ValueError` for a key not in `settings.SORT_KEYS` (no import cycle: settings imports nothing from shelf).
- `shelf/web.py`
  - `make_server(host="127.0.0.1", port=8000)` → `http.server.HTTPServer` with the handler.
  - `GET /` → 200 `text/html; charset=utf-8`: the settings page, the saved
    choice pre-checked. `?saved=1` shows a "Saved" status message.
  - `POST /` (form `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, field `sort`) → valid:
    `settings.save`, 303 redirect to `/?saved=1` (post/redirect/get). Invalid
    or missing → 400 with the page re-rendered and an error message, nothing saved.
  - Any other path → 404. Silence the default per-request stderr logging
    (`log_message` no-op).
  - All interpolated values HTML-escaped (`html.escape`).
- `shelf/cli.py`
  - `list` → prints `title - author` per book (same line format as `find`),
    ordered by `settings.load()["sort"]`.
  - `serve [--port N]` (default 8000) → binds 127.0.0.1 only, prints
    `Settings page: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` then `serve_forever()`;
    Ctrl+C exits 0 cleanly.
- README: document `list` and `serve`.
- Out of scope: browsing/editing books on the web (that is F7, deferred),
  auth, a `--sort` override flag on `list`, persisting the catalogue.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Python stdlib only; no new dependencies.
- Sort values are exactly `title` and `author`; default `title`.
- Settings file: JSON `{"sort": "<value>"}`, UTF-8; location from
  `SHELF_SETTINGS` env var, else `~/.shelf/settings.json`.
- Server binds `127.0.0.1` only.
- Tests never touch the real home dir: they set `SHELF_SETTINGS` to a tmp path
  (pytest `monkeypatch` + `tmp_path`).
- Existing tests keep passing; existing line format `title - author` unchanged.

TASKS (one build agent, in order, test-first: write the failing test, run it, see it fail, implement, see it pass):

T1 settings module — build=opus
  Files: shelf/settings.py (new), tests/test_settings.py (new)
  Tests: default is title with no file; save then load round-trips; save of
  "isbn" raises ValueError and writes nothing; corrupt JSON → default; a file
  holding `{"sort": "isbn"}` → default; parent dir is created.

T2 sorted list — build=opus
  Files: shelf/books.py, shelf/cli.py, tests/test_books.py, tests/test_cli.py (new)
  Tests: `books.sorted_books("author")` orders by author case-insensitively;
  bad key → ValueError; `cli.main(["list"])` prints in saved order (use
  capsys; seed via books.add since the catalogue is in memory, and
  settings.save to choose the order).

T3 web settings page — build=opus, UI per `## UI design`
  Files: shelf/web.py (new), shelf/cli.py (serve), tests/test_web.py (new), README.md
  Tests: start `make_server(port=0)` in a thread, use `urllib.request`:
  GET / → 200 and the saved option is `checked`; POST sort=author → 303 to
  /?saved=1 and settings.load() == author; POST sort=isbn → 400, setting
  unchanged; GET /nope → 404. Shut the server down in teardown.

VERIFICATION:
  python -m pytest -q        → all pass, exit 0
  Manual/scripted end-to-end: with SHELF_SETTINGS pointing at a temp file,
  run `python -m shelf serve --port 8765` in the background, POST sort=author
  with curl, stop the server, then a fresh `python -c` process calls
  `settings.load()` → `{'sort': 'author'}` (proves it survives a restart).

## UI design
The build agent loads skillator:design-arwen (mode build) and designs the one
page before writing T3's markup: a single self-contained HTML document, inline
CSS, no JS required, no external assets. Must have: a page title, a
`<fieldset>`/`<legend>` radio group (Title / Author) with real `<label>`s, one
submit button, a status region (`role="status"`) for "Saved", an error message
tied to the group for a 400, visible focus, works at 320px wide, respects
`prefers-color-scheme`. The build agent appends its UI decisions here.

## Decisions
Ruling: "use a single agent" = one dispatched agent for the whole build; the design file is written by the orchestrator (design seat -) and the design-arwen UI pass runs inside that same build agent rather than as a separate agent - user instruction outranks the skill's separate UI seat - cost if wrong: one more agent pass on the page.
Ruling: verify seat run by the orchestrator (opus) - running the VERIFICATION commands and reading the diff, no second agent, per the user's single-agent instruction - cost if wrong: less independent review on a small, non-critical change.
Ruling: add a `list` subcommand - it does not exist yet and the setting is meaningless without it - cost if wrong: small, the user may have meant another command.
Ruling: settings path ~/.shelf/settings.json, SHELF_SETTINGS override - per-user, survives runs, testable - cost if wrong: a one-line path change.
Ruling: stdlib http.server bound to 127.0.0.1, default port 8000, --port flag - no deps, local only - cost if wrong: trivial.
Ruling: F8 does not conflict with deferred F7 - F7 is browsing the shelf; this page only edits one setting - cost if wrong: the user may want F8 deferred with F7.

"""The catalogue, in memory."""
_BOOKS = []


def add(title, author):
    book = {"title": title, "author": author}
    _BOOKS.append(book)
    return book


def find(query):
    return [b for b in _BOOKS if query in b["title"]]


def all_books():
    return list(_BOOKS)


def clear():
    _BOOKS.clear()

import argparse

def main(argv=None):

    a = sub.add_parser("add")

import urllib.parse
import urllib.request

import pytest

from shelf import settings, web


class NoRedirect(urllib.request.HTTPRedirectHandler):
    def redirect_request(self, *a, **k):
        return None


open_url = urllib.request.build_opener(NoRedirect).open


@pytest.fixture
def base(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("SHELF_SETTINGS", str(tmp_path / "settings.json"))
    srv = web.make_server(port=0)
    t = threading.Thread(target=srv.serve_forever, daemon=True)
    t.start()
    yield "http://127.0.0.1:%d" % srv.server_address[1]
    srv.shutdown()
    srv.server_close()
    t.join()


def status(url, data=None):
    body = urllib.parse.urlencode(data).encode() if data is not None else None
    try:
        r = open_url(url, body)
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        r = e
    with r:
        return r.status, r.headers, r.read().decode("utf-8")


def test_binds_loopback_only(base):
    assert base.startswith("http://127.0.0.1:")


def test_get_checks_saved_option(base):
    settings.save("author")
    code, headers, page = status(base + "/")
    assert code == 200
    assert headers["Content-Type"] == "text/html; charset=utf-8"
    assert re.search(r'<input[^>]*value="author"[^>]*checked', page)
    assert not re.search(r'<input[^>]*value="title"[^>]*checked', page)
    assert 'role="status"' in page


def test_get_saved_shows_message(base):
    _, _, page = status(base + "/?saved=1")
    assert "Saved" in page


def test_post_valid_saves_and_redirects(base):
    code, headers, _ = status(base + "/", {"sort": "author"})
    assert code == 303
    assert headers["Location"] == "/?saved=1"
    assert settings.load() == {"sort": "author"}


def test_post_invalid_is_400_and_saves_nothing(base):
    code, _, page = status(base + "/", {"sort": "isbn"})
    assert code == 400
    assert 'role="alert"' in page or "aria-invalid" in page
    assert not settings.path().exists()
    assert settings.load() == {"sort": "title"}


def test_post_missing_is_400(base):
    code, _, _ = status(base + "/", {})
    assert code == 400


def test_unknown_path_is_404(base):
    assert status(base + "/nope")[0] == 404
    assert status(base + "/nope", {"sort": "author"})[0] == 404

1	# `build` — new UI, from nothing
2	
3	Prereq: SKILL.md Phase 0–2 done (platform, register, dials, scene sentence, Design Read,
4	direction, signature). Also read [craft.md](craft.md); product register also reads
5	[product-ui.md](product-ui.md). Finish through [verify.md](verify.md) and leave a
6	`DESIGN.md` behind. Nothing exists to preserve — if
7	something does, you want [redesign.md](redesign.md) instead.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 1. Pick the substrate before the pixels
12	
13	**Reach for a real design system when the brief implies one.** Rebuilding Carbon by hand
14	is not craft, it's waste — and the result is always subtly wrong.
15	
16	| Brief signal | System | Install |
17	|---|---|---|
18	| Google / Android-flavored web | Material Web (M3) | `npm i @material/web` |
19	| Microsoft / enterprise | Fluent UI React v9 | `npm i @fluentui/react-components` |
20	| IBM / data-heavy enterprise | Carbon | `npm i @carbon/react` |
21	| GitHub-adjacent devtool | Primer (product) / Primer Brand (marketing) | `npm i @primer/react` |
22	| UK public sector | GOV.UK Frontend | `npm i govuk-frontend` |
23	| US federal | USWDS | `npm i @uswds/uswds` |
24	| Atlassian app | Atlaskit | per-component `@atlaskit/*` |
25	| Shopify app | Polaris web components | CDN + `shopify-api-key` meta |
26	| Accessible unstyled primitives | Radix | `npm i @radix-ui/themes` |
27	| Own-the-code components | shadcn/ui | `npx shadcn@latest init` |
28	
29	**When the brief is an aesthetic, not a system** ("Linear-style", "brutalist", "premium
30	consumer", "Awwwards"), don't install a system — build tokens + primitives yourself from
31	the Phase 1 direction. A design system would flatten exactly the thing you're being paid
32	for.
33	
34	**Verify every dependency before you write an import.** Check it exists at the version you
35	name, check the API you're calling is in that version, check the component you reference
36	actually ships. Inventing a package or a prop is a shipped bug, not a typo.
37	
38	---
39	
40	## 2. Two passes — plan, critique the plan, *then* code
41	
42	The single highest-leverage habit in this skill. Do the first pass in your head or a
43	scratch note; only show the user something you're confident about.
44	
45	**Style menu first.** Unless the direction is pinned or there is no user, offer the eight
46	styles in [styles.md](styles.md), mock the ones picked, and write the plan below for the
47	style the user chooses. No user: pick one of the eight yourself and list it on
48	`Chose for you:`.
49	
50	### Pass 1 — write the plan
51	
52	Four blocks, compact:
53	
54	- **Color** — 4–6 named values in OKLCH, each with its role (`bg`, `surface`, `ink`,
55	  `muted`, `accent`, and at most one more). Name the color strategy from Phase 1.
56	- **Type** — one or two families: a characterful display face used with restraint and a
57	  body face, or one family across weights. If two, make them clearly distinct. No default
58	  third mono "for captions or data" — small mono labels are template chrome; numbers
59	  align with `tabular-nums`. Mono only for literal code or IDs, logged as `Deliberate:`.
60	  Name the scale ratio.
61	- **Layout** — one-sentence prose per section, plus an **ASCII wireframe** for anything
62	  non-obvious. Wireframes are cheap; they expose a repetitive rhythm before you've written
63	  400 lines of CSS. **Say the alignment per section** (left, centred, justified) — left
64	  unstated it comes out centred everywhere. Brand register: name what the hero opens with,
65	  the most characteristic thing in the subject's world (an object, a live demo, a moment),
66	  not a metric row.
67	- **Signature** — the one sentence from Phase 2, and where in the layout it lands.
68	
69	### Pass 2 — critique the plan against the brief
70	
71	Before any code: work through a *similar* prompt in your head and see where you land. If
72	any block of your plan is where you'd land anyway — that's the training-data default, not
73	a choice for this brief. **Revise that block and say what you changed and why.**
74	
75	**Then get one lens that is not yours.** Self-critique in your own head produces the
76	rationalisation you would predict — it did exactly that when this skill was run
77	end-to-end. Dispatch **one** subagent, the UX & interaction / a11y seat from
78	`redesign.md` §3, briefed with the plan and its lens only, and ask it for the top 3
79	problems ranked plus its non-negotiables. One seat, not a panel: `build` is a fresh
80	surface with no audit evidence to spread across three lenses, and a second visual seat
81	would only agree with you.
82	
83	Where it conflicts with your plan, **decide** and say why in one line — the seat advises,
84	you own the route. No delegate mechanism on this host, or no budget for it? Say
85	`critique: self only` in the plan so the reader knows which kind of critique it survived.
86	Never report a self-critique as if a second lens had passed it.
87	
88	Run the three-saturated-looks check here, not after the code exists — and, **in the brand
89	register only**, the SKILL.md category-reflex check (both altitudes). In the product
90	register that check is off (SKILL.md Phase 1): test the signature as one systematic UX
91	device instead, and do not rework toward unguessability.
92	
93	Only once the plan survives its own critique do you write code — and then you follow it
94	exactly, deriving every color and type value from it.
95	
96	**Optional visual gate:** if the user would rather move boxes than read prose, publish the
97	plan as artboards first — see [canvas.md](canvas.md).
98	
99	---
100	
101	## 3. Walking skeleton before breadth
102	
103	Build **one surface fully to spec** — real content, all eight states, signature present,
104	responsive, verified in the browser or on the device. It proves the route for a tenth of
105	the cost of proving it across six screens. Then widen.
106	
107	---
108	
109	## 4. Build out with subagents
110	
111	For anything multi-surface, implement via subagents rather than one linear pass.
112	
113	- **Slice by surface or workflow.** One subagent owns one screen / flow / component
114	  end to end.
115	- **Brief every agent identically on the shared system** — the resolved direction, the
116	  signature and its rules, the token values, and the craft.md bar. Independently built
117	  surfaces drifting apart is *the* failure mode; the shared written brief is what keeps
118	  them one product.
119	- **Isolate parallel file edits.** Agents touching the same tree concurrently → give each
120	  a git worktree (`isolation`) so they don't collide; otherwise sequence them. This holds
121	  on every host, including ones that run agents in the working tree with no sandbox.
122	- **No delegation on this host?** Build the surfaces sequentially in one session off the
123	  same written brief. Slower, identical output — the brief on disk is what matters, not
124	  the parallelism.
125	- **Each agent runs its own ship gate and returns evidence** (a real render or
126	  screenshot), not a claim. You reconcile, check cross-surface consistency, and relay.
127	
128	---
129	
130	## 5. Stack defaults (when the user hasn't picked one)
131	
132	Only defaults — an existing project's stack always wins.
133	
134	- React + TypeScript + Vite; Tailwind for utility, CSS custom properties for tokens.
135	- Local state first. Reach for a store only when two distant components genuinely share
136	  state; never install one for a landing page.
137	- No CSS-in-JS runtime for a static page.
138	- Dark mode via a `data-theme` attribute or `prefers-color-scheme`, with tokens redefined —
139	  never a second hand-maintained stylesheet.
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 6. Finish
144	
145	Run the SKILL.md **ship gate** — the single gate, tagged `static`/`browser`/`delegated`.
146	No browser? Run every `static` item anyway and report in SKILL.md's terminal-state shape.
147	Do not report done on an unrendered page.

- Outside the repo: I added the UI decisions under `## UI design` in `...\scratchpad\f100\design-2026-10-26-settings-page.md`.

**2. Tests** (`python -m pytest -q` each time)
- **Starting point:** 3 passed.
- **T1:** the new test file failed to load because `shelf.settings` didn't exist yet. After implementing, 9 passed.
- **T2:** 4 failed (`sorted_books` missing; `list` exited with an argument error). After implementing, 13 passed.
- **T3, web page:** the new test file failed to load because `shelf.web` didn't exist yet. After implementing, 1 failed: a POST to `/nope` got a connection reset on Windows. Once the request body is read before the 404, 20 passed.
- **T3, `serve` command:** its test failed first, then 21 passed. Final lines:
  ```
  .....................                                                    [100%]
  21 passed in 4.66s
  ```
- **End-to-end:** with `SHELF_SETTINGS` pointing at a temp file I started `python -m shelf serve --port 8765`.
  - POST `sort=author` returned 303 to `/?saved=1`, and GET `/nope` returned 404.
  - After stopping the server, a fresh process printed `{'sort': 'author'}`. Port 8765 is closed, so no server is left running.
  - The server exited with code 1 because I killed it directly, not with Ctrl+C. The clean Ctrl+C exit is covered by a unit test.

**3. UI decisions:** a plain, conventional page: system font, one blue accent, light and dark colours. The Title and Author choices are full-width cards with a visible focus outline. Each card shows a two-line preview of what `shelf list` prints in that order, and the "Saved" message names that command. The page also shows where the settings file lives. I checked the colour contrast by calculation and it passes in both themes. Headless Edge produced no screenshots here.

**4. Deviations from the spec**
- **Extra tests:** a missing `sort` field returns 400, and a test for `serve` swaps out the real server to check it binds 127.0.0.1, prints the URL and exits 0 on Ctrl+C. The spec didn't list these, but `serve` needed a test to be done test-first.
- **Imports:** `books.py` imports `settings`, which the spec allows. `cli.py` imports `web` only when `serve` runs.
- **Body read first:** POST handling reads the request body before checking the path, to fix the Windows connection reset above.
- **Error message:** on a 400 the fieldset also gets `aria-invalid`.

1	"""User settings, a small JSON file. SHELF_SETTINGS overrides the location."""
2	import json
3	import os
4	import tempfile
5	from pathlib import Path
6	
7	SORT_KEYS = ("title", "author")
8	DEFAULTS = {"sort": "title"}
9	
10	
11	def path():
12	    env = os.environ.get("SHELF_SETTINGS")
13	    return Path(env) if env else Path.home() / ".shelf" / "settings.json"
14	
15	
16	def load():
17	    out = dict(DEFAULTS)
18	    try:
19	        data = json.loads(path().read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
20	    except (OSError, ValueError):
21	        return out
22	    if isinstance(data, dict) and data.get("sort") in SORT_KEYS:
23	        out["sort"] = data["sort"]
24	    return out
25	
26	
27	def save(sort):
28	    if sort not in SORT_KEYS:
29	        raise ValueError("sort must be one of %s" % ", ".join(SORT_KEYS))
30	    p = path()
31	    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
32	    data = {"sort": sort}
33	    # atomic: temp file in the same dir, then replace
34	    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=p.parent, prefix=".settings-", suffix=".tmp")
35	    try:
36	        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
37	            json.dump(data, f)
38	        os.replace(tmp, p)
39	    except BaseException:
40	        os.unlink(tmp)
41	        raise
42	    return data

"""F8 end-to-end: save via the served page, stop the server, read back in a new process."""
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

repo = sys.argv[1]
env = dict(os.environ, SHELF_SETTINGS=os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "settings.json"))
url = "http://127.0.0.1:8766/"


class NoRedirect(urllib.request.HTTPRedirectHandler):
    def redirect_request(self, *a):
        return None


opener = urllib.request.build_opener(NoRedirect)


def hit(data=None, path=""):
    try:
        r = opener.open(url + path, data=data, timeout=5)
        return r.status, r.headers.get("Location"), r.read().decode()
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        return e.code, e.headers.get("Location"), e.read().decode()


srv = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-m", "shelf", "serve", "--port", "8766"],
                       cwd=repo, env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
try:
    print("server says:", srv.stdout.readline().strip())
    for _ in range(20):
        try:
            hit()
            break
        except OSError:
            time.sleep(0.25)
    code, _, body = hit()
    print("GET /", code, "title checked:", 'value="title" checked' in body)
    code, loc, _ = hit(b"sort=author")
    print("POST sort=author", code, "->", loc)
    code, _, _ = hit(b"sort=isbn")
    print("POST sort=isbn", code)
    code, _, body = hit(path="?saved=1")
    print("GET /?saved=1", code, "author checked:", 'value="author" checked' in body,
          "| Saved shown:", "Saved." in body)
finally:
    srv.terminate()
    srv.wait()
print("server stopped")
out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", "from shelf import settings; print(settings.load())"],
                     cwd=repo, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
print("new process load():", out.stdout.strip())
lst = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "shelf", "list"], cwd=repo, env=env,
                     capture_output=True, text=True)
print("shelf list exit:", lst.returncode)

The settings page works. `python -m shelf serve` opens a local page where you pick Title or Author, and `python -m shelf list` uses that choice on later runs. All 21 tests pass. I also ran the full flow myself: started the server, saved "author" through the page, stopped the server, and a fresh process read back `{'sort': 'author'}`. Nothing is committed yet.

**What was added**
- **`list` command:** there wasn't one before, so I added it. It prints `title - author` lines, sorted by the saved choice and ignoring capitals.
- **`serve [--port N]`:** serves the page on `127.0.0.1` only (default port 8000), using only Python's standard library. A bad value gets an error page and nothing is saved; Ctrl+C stops the server.
- **Where the choice is saved:** `~/.shelf/settings.json`, or another file if you set `SHELF_SETTINGS`. A missing or broken file falls back to Title. The tests use a temporary file, never your home folder.
- **The page:** a plain form with light and dark colours, keyboard focus outlines, and a "Saved" message. Each option shows a two-line preview of how `list` would print.
- **Files:** new `shelf/settings.py`, `shelf/web.py` and three test files; changes to `shelf/books.py`, `shelf/cli.py`, `tests/test_books.py` and `README.md`.

**Decisions I made**
- I read "use a single agent" as one build agent in total. So I wrote the design myself, the page design was done inside that same agent, and I did the checking.
- This doesn't clash with the deferred F7 (web UI for browsing the shelf), because this page only changes one setting.
- The design notes are in `scratchpad/f100/design-2026-10-26-settings-page.md`.

**Worth knowing**
- **Look of the page not checked:** nobody has looked at it in a browser. The 320px width, dark mode and focus outlines are written in but unchecked; the agent only checked colour contrast by calculation.
- **Any website can change the setting:** while `serve` is running, a page open in your browser could send a form to `127.0.0.1:8000` and change it. That only switches the sort order, so I left it; checking the request's `Origin` header would close it.
- **`list` is empty from the command line:** the catalogue only lives in memory, so `add` in one run is gone by the next `list`. That was already true before this change.
- **Untracked `__pycache__/` folders:** the repo has no `.gitignore`, so they show up in `git status`.
- **Leftover files outside the repo:** the agent's screenshot folder `scratchpad/f8shots/` and my check script `scratchpad/f100/e2e_f8.py`. Both are safe to delete.

F8 is marked done on the board in `TICKETS.md`. Do you want me to commit it, with the board change in the same commit?

GOAL: `python -m shelf serve` serves a small local web page where a member picks
the default sort of `list` (title or author); the choice is saved to disk and
`python -m shelf list` uses it on later runs.

CHOSEN: stdlib only (`http.server`, `json`, `pathlib`) — the project has no
dependencies and no build. A new `shelf/settings.py` owns load/save of a JSON
file; a new `shelf/web.py` owns the HTTP handler; `cli.py` gains `list` and
`serve`. `list` does not exist yet, so it is added here (it is the thing the
setting controls).

DESIGN:
- `shelf/settings.py`
  - `SORT_KEYS = ("title", "author")`, `DEFAULTS = {"sort": "title"}`
  - `path()` → `Path(os.environ["SHELF_SETTINGS"])` if set, else
    `Path.home() / ".shelf" / "settings.json"`.
  - `load()` → dict: DEFAULTS merged with the file. Missing file, unreadable
    file, invalid JSON, or a `sort` value not in SORT_KEYS → that key falls back
    to its default (never raises).
  - `save(sort)` → validates (`ValueError` if not in SORT_KEYS), creates the
    parent dir, writes `{"sort": sort}` as UTF-8 JSON atomically (write a temp
    file in the same dir, then `os.replace`). Returns the saved dict.
- `shelf/books.py`: `sorted_books(key)` → `sorted(all_books(), key=lambda b: b[key].casefold())`;
  `ValueError` for a key not in `settings.SORT_KEYS` (no import cycle: settings imports nothing from shelf).
- `shelf/web.py`
  - `make_server(host="127.0.0.1", port=8000)` → `http.server.HTTPServer` with the handler.
  - `GET /` → 200 `text/html; charset=utf-8`: the settings page, the saved
    choice pre-checked. `?saved=1` shows a "Saved" status message.
  - `POST /` (form `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, field `sort`) → valid:
    `settings.save`, 303 redirect to `/?saved=1` (post/redirect/get). Invalid
    or missing → 400 with the page re-rendered and an error message, nothing saved.
  - Any other path → 404. Silence the default per-request stderr logging
    (`log_message` no-op).
  - All interpolated values HTML-escaped (`html.escape`).
- `shelf/cli.py`
  - `list` → prints `title - author` per book (same line format as `find`),
    ordered by `settings.load()["sort"]`.
  - `serve [--port N]` (default 8000) → binds 127.0.0.1 only, prints
    `Settings page: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` then `serve_forever()`;
    Ctrl+C exits 0 cleanly.
- README: document `list` and `serve`.
- Out of scope: browsing/editing books on the web (that is F7, deferred),
  auth, a `--sort` override flag on `list`, persisting the catalogue.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Python stdlib only; no new dependencies.
- Sort values are exactly `title` and `author`; default `title`.
- Settings file: JSON `{"sort": "<value>"}`, UTF-8; location from
  `SHELF_SETTINGS` env var, else `~/.shelf/settings.json`.
- Server binds `127.0.0.1` only.
- Tests never touch the real home dir: they set `SHELF_SETTINGS` to a tmp path
  (pytest `monkeypatch` + `tmp_path`).
- Existing tests keep passing; existing line format `title - author` unchanged.

T1 settings module — build=opus
  Files: shelf/settings.py (new), tests/test_settings.py (new)
  Tests: default is title with no file; save then load round-trips; save of
  "isbn" raises ValueError and writes nothing; corrupt JSON → default; a file
  holding `{"sort": "isbn"}` → default; parent dir is created.

T2 sorted list — build=opus
  Files: shelf/books.py, shelf/cli.py, tests/test_books.py, tests/test_cli.py (new)
  Tests: `books.sorted_books("author")` orders by author case-insensitively;
  bad key → ValueError; `cli.main(["list"])` prints in saved order (use
  capsys; seed via books.add since the catalogue is in memory, and

  Files: shelf/web.py (new), shelf/cli.py (serve), tests/test_web.py (new), README.md
  Tests: start `make_server(port=0)` in a thread, use `urllib.request`:

## UI design
The build agent loads skillator:design-arwen (mode build) and designs the one
page before writing T3's markup: a single self-contained HTML document, inline
CSS, no JS required, no external assets. Must have: a page title, a
`<fieldset>`/`<legend>` radio group (Title / Author) with real `<label>`s, one
submit button, a status region (`role="status"`) for "Saved", an error message
tied to the group for a 400, visible focus, works at 320px wide, respects
`prefers-color-scheme`. The build agent appends its UI decisions here.

## Decisions
Ruling: "use a single agent" = one dispatched agent for the whole build; the design file is written by the orchestrator (design seat -) and the design-arwen UI pass runs inside that same build agent rather than as a separate agent - user instruction outranks the skill's separate UI seat - cost if wrong: one more agent pass on the page.
Ruling: verify seat run by the orchestrator (opus) - running the VERIFICATION commands and reading the diff, no second agent, per the user's single-agent instruction - cost if wrong: less independent review on a small, non-critical change.
Ruling: add a `list` subcommand - it does not exist yet and the setting is meaningless without it - cost if wrong: small, the user may have meant another command.
Ruling: settings path ~/.shelf/settings.json, SHELF_SETTINGS override - per-user, survives runs, testable - cost if wrong: a one-line path change.
Ruling: stdlib http.server bound to 127.0.0.1, default port 8000, --port flag - no deps, local only - cost if wrong: trivial.
Ruling: F8 does not conflict with deferred F7 - F7 is browsing the shelf; this page only edits one setting - cost if wrong: the user may want F8 deferred with F7.

The settings page works. `python -m shelf serve` opens a local page where you pick Title or Author, and `python -m shelf list` uses that choice on later runs. All 21 tests pass. I also ran the full flow myself: started the server, saved "author" through the page, stopped the server, and a fresh process read back `{'sort': 'author'}`. Nothing is committed yet.

**What was added**
- **`list` command:** there wasn't one before, so I added it. It prints `title - author` lines, sorted by the saved choice and ignoring capitals.
- **`serve [--port N]`:** serves the page on `127.0.0.1` only (default port 8000), using only Python's standard library. A bad value gets an error page and nothing is saved; Ctrl+C stops the server.
- **Where the choice is saved:** `~/.shelf/settings.json`, or another file if you set `SHELF_SETTINGS`. A missing or broken file falls back to Title. The tests use a temporary file, never your home folder.
- **The page:** a plain form with light and dark colours, keyboard focus outlines, and a "Saved" message. Each option shows a two-line preview of how `list` would print.
- **Files:** new `shelf/settings.py`, `shelf/web.py` and three test files; changes to `shelf/books.py`, `shelf/cli.py`, `tests/test_books.py` and `README.md`.

**Decisions I made**
- I read "use a single agent" as one build agent in total. So I wrote the design myself, the page design was done inside that same agent, and I did the checking.
- This doesn't clash with the deferred F7 (web UI for browsing the shelf), because this page only changes one setting.
- The design notes are in `scratchpad/f100/design-2026-10-26-settings-page.md`.

**Worth knowing**
- **Look of the page not checked:** nobody has looked at it in a browser. The 320px width, dark mode and focus outlines are written in but unchecked; the agent only checked colour contrast by calculation.
- **Any website can change the setting:** while `serve` is running, a page open in your browser could send a form to `127.0.0.1:8000` and change it. That only switches the sort order, so I left it; checking the request's `Origin` header would close it.
- **`list` is empty from the command line:** the catalogue only lives in memory, so `add` in one run is gone by the next `list`. That was already true before this change.
- **Untracked `__pycache__/` folders:** the repo has no `.gitignore`, so they show up in `git status`.
- **Leftover files outside the repo:** the agent's screenshot folder `scratchpad/f8shots/` and my check script `scratchpad/f100/e2e_f8.py`. Both are safe to delete.
